requirement: Describe the prospective randomized parallel two-condition Stage IB trial in adult daily smokers with recent panic attacks, comparing common Panic and Smoking Reduction Treatment plus nicotine replacement therapy with d-cycloserine versus matching placebo augmentation.
acceptable_values: adult daily smokers with panic attacks
PSRT plus nicotine replacement in both groups

evidence.text: The protocol defines the prospective randomized PSRT+DCS versus PSRT+PBO comparison, its smoker-with-panic population and common PSRT/NRT treatment.
The power section characterizes the study as Stage IB.

requirement: Specify individual random-number-generator assignment to PSRT+DCS or PSRT+PBO under biostatistician control, with pharmacy labels A/B, participants and study personnel blinded, and only the biostatistician able to break the blind.

evidence.text: The protocol identifies the random-number generator, biostatistician, blinded labels and code access.

requirement: Represent the treatment contrast accurately: both groups receive seven weeks of PSRT and nicotine patches, while identical capsules contain 250 mg d-cycloserine or placebo and are observed one hour before Sessions 3, 4 and 5.

evidence.text: The intervention schedule gives common PSRT/NRT and identical DCS or placebo capsules before Sessions 3-5.

requirement: Define smoking point-prevalence abstinence as the primary repeated binary outcome, specifically self-reported abstinence for at least seven days before each scheduled follow-up with objective verification overriding self-report in the conservative direction.

evidence.text: The protocol names PPA as primary and defines seven-day abstinence with conservative biochemical override.

requirement: Operationalize biochemical confirmation of stated abstinence at Weeks 8, 10, 16 and 24: saliva cotinine for reports of at least two weeks of abstinence using the stated 10 mg/ml cutoff, and expired-air carbon monoxide for 24 hours to two weeks using an 8 ppm cutoff; values above a cutoff indicate smoking.

evidence.text: The smoking-status section specifies the follow-ups, duration-dependent cotinine/CO verification and cutoffs.

notes: The protocol prints the cotinine unit as mg/ml; expert review should confirm whether the intended conventional unit is ng/ml without silently changing the source.

requirement: Define time to first smoking lapse and time to relapse as primary time-to-event outcomes from Timeline Follow-Back data collected at each follow-up, with relapse defined as the seventh day on which smoking occurs.

evidence.text: The protocol names both time-to-event outcomes and defines relapse as the seventh smoking day using TLFB.

requirement: Align repeated smoking and psychological outcomes to baseline, weekly treatment assessments and follow-ups 2, 4, 8, 10, 16 and 24 weeks after the quit date; distinguish post-quit week from overall study week when presenting visits.
acceptable_values: study week distinguished from post-quit week

evidence.text: The aims and assessment schedule define baseline, weekly treatment and six post-quit follow-ups.

requirement: Analyze the prespecified longitudinal psychological outcomes representing withdrawal symptoms, negative affect, panic severity, distress intolerance and anxiety sensitivity, and preserve their role as secondary or mechanistic outcomes rather than additional confirmatory smoking endpoints.

evidence.text: The protocol names and defines the five psychological mediator/outcome domains.
The analysis document assigns these continuous domains to longitudinal MLMs.

requirement: Define the primary efficacy population and preserve randomized assignment in treatment attribution; explicitly resolve whether all randomized participants are included regardless of treatment attendance, capsule receipt, nicotine-patch adherence, smoking after quit day or post-baseline data availability.

evidence.text: The protocol defines randomization and adherence procedures but does not define an analysis population or treatment attribution rule.

requirement: State the treatment-effect estimands for repeated PPA and time to lapse/relapse, including target population, treatment contrast, outcome variable, time horizon and strategies for treatment discontinuation, nonadherence, resumed smoking, prohibited cessation treatment and death; flag each unresolved intercurrent-event strategy for confirmation.

evidence.text: The protocol defines the contrasts and outcomes and allows continued cessation attempts after lapse, but does not formalize estimands or all intercurrent-event strategies.

requirement: Before outcome modeling, summarize key baseline demographic, smoking and psychological variables by group, inspect outcome distributions and missing/dropout patterns, transform measures when necessary, and include baseline variables showing treatment-group imbalance as covariates.

evidence.text: The overview defines baseline equivalence checks, covariate selection, missingness inspection and transformations.

requirement: Analyze repeated PPA with a logistic generalized linear mixed model, nesting repeated observations within participants and participants within treatment cohort, and estimate treatment differences in the rate of PPA change and at prespecified assessment points.
acceptable_values: treatment difference in rate of change

evidence.text: The plan specifies logistic GLMM, the three-level nesting and both slope and assessment-specific treatment contrasts.

requirement: For PPA time course, compare quadratic and exponential parameterizations using AIC and BIC, document the selected form, and center time at a requested assessment such as Week 24 when estimating the treatment contrast at that point.

evidence.text: The PPA analysis selects quadratic versus exponential time by AIC/BIC and centers time for visit-specific comparisons.

requirement: Compare treatment conditions on risk and time to first lapse and relapse using Cox proportional-hazards models; report hazard ratios with confidence intervals and specify event origins, censoring, ties and proportional-hazards diagnostics before finalization.

evidence.text: The plan specifies Cox comparisons of relative risk and time to lapse and relapse but does not operationalize censoring or diagnostics.

requirement: Use longitudinal multilevel models analogous to the PPA model for withdrawal symptoms, negative affect, panic severity, distress intolerance and anxiety sensitivity, with treatment-by-time contrasts and relevant control variables.

evidence.text: The plan assigns the five continuous psychological domains to MLMs analogous to the PPA GLMM.

requirement: Evaluate moderated mediation separately by treatment condition: estimate longitudinal treatment-specific change in each mediator as path a, include all mediators simultaneously in the PPA GLMM for path b, derive the PPA treatment path as path c, and assess mediated pathways with Bayesian bootstrap mediation.
acceptable_values: path b simultaneous mediators in PPA GLMM

evidence.text: Aim 3 defines treatment-specific a paths, simultaneous b paths, the c path and Bayesian bootstrap mediated-path testing.

requirement: Define the primary handling of missing PPA, unknown biochemical confirmation, incomplete Timeline Follow-Back and missing psychological scores under an explicit missingness assumption; do not treat the reference sensitivity analysis as a substitute for a primary missing-data rule.

evidence.text: The protocol defines verification and repeated assessments but not primary rules for missing smoking or scale data.
The reference supplies only pattern-mixture sensitivity language, not an operational primary missing-data rule.

requirement: Assess missing-data robustness with pattern-mixture models that distinguish complete cases, sporadic missingness and dropout and estimate whether the PSRT+DCS versus PSRT+PBO contrast varies by missing-data pattern.

evidence.text: The missing-data section calls for pattern-mixture reruns by complete, sporadic and dropout patterns.

requirement: Resolve the inferential hierarchy and multiplicity strategy across repeated PPA contrasts, two time-to-smoking-event outcomes, five psychological domains and multiple mediated pathways; identify which tests are confirmatory versus exploratory and state the alpha and interval conventions.

evidence.text: The protocol specifies three aims and many outcomes but gives no hierarchy, alpha or multiplicity control.
The reference maps analyses to aims but also omits alpha and multiplicity control.

requirement: Preserve the prospective target of 80 participants and the Stage IB objective of feasibility and deciding whether a Stage II study is warranted; do not replace this target with the registry's later actual enrollment.

evidence.text: The protocol states a target enrollment of 80.
The prospective power section uses n=80 and frames the Stage IB feasibility/Stage II objective.

requirement: Document the PPA Monte Carlo sensitivity assumptions: n=80, an average five post-quit assessments per participant, 27% final PPA for PSRT+PBO, 1,000 simulations per candidate rate, and 80% power when final PSRT+DCS PPA is at least 43%.

evidence.text: The power analysis gives the Monte Carlo sample, assessment, control-rate, simulation and detectable-rate assumptions.

requirement: Define a safety population and summarize adverse and serious adverse events by randomized treatment, severity, seriousness, relationship, action and discontinuation, together with vital signs, clinically indicated laboratory tests, pregnancy tests and prespecified DCS/nicotine-patch side effects.

evidence.text: The protocol defines safety assessments, risks, AE/SAE characterization and reporting but not a statistical safety population or display conventions.

requirement: Before finalization, expose unresolved operational choices including randomization ratio or blocking, scale scoring and partial-item rules, analysis windows, covariance and random-effects structure, cohort definition, small-sample inference, covariate-selection threshold, model convergence fallbacks, Cox censoring and mediation bootstrap settings.

evidence.text: The protocol defines design, measures and visits but leaves these statistical implementation choices open.
The terse reference plan names models and power assumptions without resolving these implementation details.
